subject: Processing Addendum - subprocessor safeguards & counsel flags (round 1-2)
messages:
From: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@medisync.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Ross <evan.ross@medisync.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing addendum - initial redlines

Hi Olga —

Thanks for sending the template. Attached is our round 1 redline (Medisync_DPA_Redlines_Round1.docx). Two items our counsel flagged as high-priority:

1) Subprocessor notification window — we asked to shorten notice from 30 to 10 days for any new subprocessors processing PHI.
2) Cross-border transfers — we'd like explicit reference to UK adequacy plus standard contractual clauses where applicable.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a subprocessor inventory CSV and evidence of SOC 2 coverage for the infra subproc? Evan (cc'd) will lead on the legal follow-up.

Proposed next step: Redwood to provide an annotated response to the redline and an execution plan (DocuSign vs AdobeSign).

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Barnes
Head of Compliance, Medisync
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@medisync.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing addendum - initial redlines

Claire —

Acknowledged, thanks for the redline. I've uploaded your doc and pulled the primary flags into an internal note. Short answers up front:

- Subprocessor inventory: yes, we can provide the CSV (attached subprocessor_matrix_2025Q3.csv) and we'll include the deployment (region) column.
- SOC 2 evidence: we can share our SOC 2 Type II attestation; we'll provide an extracted controls summary for the infra subprocessor.

Two items for internal alignment before I prepare our annotated counter:
1) Notice window: Aditya — legal preference on 10 vs 30 day notification for PHI-handling subprocessors? We typically push back to 30 but can agree to 14 in a limited carveout.
2) Transfers: Naomi — confirm if Redwood can commit to SCCs + adequacy referencing (UK), and note whether we need an EU-US Addendum for US-hosted infra.

Plan: I'll circulate an internal counsel digest today, prepare a response (Redwood_DPA_Redlines_Round2.pdf) and propose routing via DocuSign with in-person exec for the SOW afterward.

Cheers,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing addendum - internal: notice window + subproc carveouts

Olga —

Quick take from legal: 10 days is too aggressive operationally given our onboarding cadence; 30 days is standard. Compromise we can offer: 14 days limited to "critical" subprocessors (those handling PHI or persistent KV cache storage). For non-critical subprocessors we keep the 30 day notice.

Also recommend: add a paragraph describing our right to continue servicing on legacy subprocessors for a 60-day transition to avoid availability issues.

I'll annotate the clause in the redline and flag where we should propose the 14/30 split.

- Aditya
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing addendum - transfers and SCCs

Olga / Aditya —

On transfers: we can accept explicit reference to UK adequacy and apply SCCs for transfers from the EEA to the US. Operational note: our standard approach is to include an EU-US Addendum when customers require contractual guarantees; it's an additional doc but quick to attach. For Medisync I'll prepare a short blurb that references the SCCs + the optional Addendum if they prefer.

Evidence: I'll attach a one-page summary of the control mappings (SOC-2 extract) to accompany the redline.

Naomi
Privacy & Compliance
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@medisync.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@medisync.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood response to Medisync redline (round 2) + execution plan

Claire / Evan —

Attached is our annotated counter (Redwood_DPA_Redlines_Round2.pdf) and the subprocessor inventory CSV. Summary of changes and proposals:

- Notification window: propose 14 days for critical subprocessors (PHI/KV cache) and 30 days for others. We added a 60-day transition carveout.
- Transfers: we accept UK adequacy reference and commit to SCCs where applicable. We can attach an EU-US Addendum if Medisync would like binding language.
- Evidence: attached SOC 2 extract (controls summary) and a one-pager from Naomi.

Execution: recommend DocuSign (we have an enterprise envelope template). I'll include Marcelo from ops to confirm infrastructure sign-off if required. Please confirm the signer list and whether Medisync prefers AdobeSign.

Next steps:
- If you accept the annotated counter, we'll prepare DocuSign envelope and route for signature (targeting next week).
- If further legal redlines, Evan, please return them and we can do a short call.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_Round2.pdf, subprocessor_matrix_2025Q3.csv, esign_instructions.txt

Best,
Olga
From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@medisync.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@medisync.com>, kjefferson@clarklaw.com
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 11:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood response to Medisync redline (round 2) + execution plan

Olga —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments. Two follow-up items from our counsel: 

1) Subprocessor carveout language: could you make the 60-day transition explicit that it does not reduce Medisync's termination rights if a new subprocessor materially degrades security or compliance? Counsel prefers a one-sentence carveout exception.
2) DocuSign: Medisync requires signer identity verification via SMS or phone challenge on the DocuSign envelope (we'll share the account settings). Is Redwood able to enforce that on your template?

If you can accept the two items, we'll confirm the final signer list and proceed with DocuSign.

Evan Ross
General Counsel, Medisync
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@medisync.com>, Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@medisync.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood response to Medisync redline (round 2) + execution plan

Evan / Claire —

Acknowledged. We can: 

1) Add the explicit carveout sentence to the 60-day transition clause to preserve your termination rights for material security/compliance degradation. Aditya will draft the one-liner.
2) DocuSign verification: yes, Redwood can require an SMS/phone challenge on the envelope. I'll coordinate with our ops team to apply the verification setting and will confirm once the envelope is prepared.

I'll incorporate Evan's two items into a v2 redline and send the final DocuSign link once the signer list is confirmed. Target: envelope out by Tue, 2025-10-14.

Thanks,
Olga
